passage: When the first working transistor was demonstrated at Bell Laboratories in 1947, it was a fragile laboratory curiosity. Yet the device did something the vacuum tubes of the day could not do efficiently: it switched and amplified electrical signals using a small sliver of doped semiconductor rather than a heated, power-hungry, easily broken glass tube. Over the following decade, engineers learned to make transistors smaller, cheaper, and more reliable, and to pack many of them onto a single chip of silicon. The historian of technology who traces this arc argues that the transistor's lasting significance lies not in any one application but in a shift of medium—from the vacuum tube to the solid-state device—that made compact, durable, mass-produced electronics possible for the first time.
question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: The first transistor demonstrated at Bell Laboratories in 1947 was too fragile to be used in any setting outside of the controlled environment of the research laboratory itself.
The transistor's lasting importance lies in replacing the vacuum tube with a compact solid-state device, a shift of medium that made cheap, durable, mass-produced electronics possible.
Engineers in the decade after 1947 succeeded in packing many transistors onto a single chip of silicon.
Vacuum tubes were inefficient because they relied on heated glass components that consumed large amounts of power.

explanation: Choice B is correct. The passage builds toward the historian's claim that the transistor matters not for any single use but for a change of medium—from the power-hungry, fragile vacuum tube to the small solid-state device—that made compact, cheap, durable, mass-produced electronics possible. Choice B captures that thesis. Choice A reports only the opening detail about the first transistor's fragility. Choice C and Choice D each restate a supporting fact (later miniaturization; the tube's inefficiency) without reaching the main point the passage is organized around.
